payload.task_text:
I am a research librarian doing a cross-reference analysis between two academic databases. I need to compare the papers available in the Scholarly database (specifically the arxiv_papers collection) with those in the arxiv database to find overlapping papers and understand coverage differences.

Please create an Excel file called "Citation_Cross_Reference.xlsx" in my workspace with three sheets.

The first sheet, "Scholarly_Papers", should list all papers from the Scholarly arxiv_papers collection with columns: Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Year, Journal_Ref. Published_Year is the four-digit year of the paper's published date. Authors should be listed as a single comma-separated string.

The second sheet, "Arxiv_Papers", should list all papers from the arxiv database with columns: Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Year, Categories. Published_Year is the four-digit year of the paper's published date. Categories should be a comma-separated string.

The third sheet, "Overlap_Analysis", should contain every paper that appears in either database (the union), matched by paper ID, with columns: Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly (Yes/No), In_Arxiv (Yes/No). A paper present in both is marked Yes/Yes; a paper only in Scholarly is Yes/No; a paper only in arxiv is No/Yes.

After creating the spreadsheet, please send an email summarizing the findings to research-lead@university.edu with the subject "Cross-Reference Analysis: Scholarly vs Arxiv Paper Databases". The email body should mention the total number of papers in each database, the number of overlapping papers, and highlight any papers that are unique to one database.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. The task-scoped collections are smaller than the exposed per-call bounds, so make exactly two native-parallel source calls: `search-arxiv(keyword="")` for the complete Scholarly `arxiv_papers` collection and `search_papers(query="", max_results=50)` for the complete local arXiv collection. Do not issue topic-by-topic searches. Normalize authors and years, deduplicate only by exact Paper_ID, and construct the exact source rows plus the exact-ID union and Yes/No flags in memory. Create `Citation_Cross_Reference.xlsx` once with sheets named exactly `Scholarly_Papers`, `Arxiv_Papers`, and `Overlap_Analysis`, using one bulk write per sheet and one read-back. Then send exactly one email to `research-lead@university.edu` with subject `Cross-Reference Analysis: Scholarly vs Arxiv Paper Databases` and the three verified population counts plus unique-paper highlights.

nodes.text:
I need the complete list of papers in the Scholarly database's `arxiv_papers` collection.

Background: The Scholarly database is accessed through MCP tools with the `mcp__scholarly__` prefix. I know there is a `search-arxiv` tool, but calling it with an empty keyword fails with "Missing keyword". There may be other listing/enumeration tools on the same Scholarly MCP server (e.g. tools matching names like list, read, get, query, select, directory_tree, list_allowed_directories, count, info, etc.) that can return the full arxiv_papers collection.

Your task: Explore the Scholarly MCP server and find a way to enumerate and return EVERY paper in the `arxiv_papers` collection (do not do topic-by-topic keyword searches). If `search-arxiv` is the only way, figure out the minimal set of calls needed to retrieve all papers in that collection.

Report back with:
1. How many papers are in the scholarly arxiv_papers collection total.
2. For EACH paper: its Paper ID, Title, Authors (as a list), published date (full date string), and Journal_Ref (if any).
3. The exact field names returned by the collection so I know whether the "journal_ref" field is named journal/ref/journal_ref.

Be complete and precise — list every single paper. Return the raw data for all papers.
Enumerate scholarly arxiv papers
